  "outcome_variable": "department_goal_achievement",
  "per_column": [
    {"name": "goal_scope_domain", "causal_role": "confounder", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "The domain of the goal (revenue vs satisfaction) plausibly varies by department and independently affects how achievable the goal is; a common cause of both departmental context and achievement."},
    {"name": "intervention_mechanism_type", "causal_role": "treatment", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "The intervention/mechanism applied (market expansion, process automation) is the candidate cause whose effect on achievement is being attributed."},
    {"name": "goal_quantification_specificity", "causal_role": "confounder", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "How specifically the goal is quantified can shape both the type of intervention chosen and measured achievement; a plausible common cause not on the causal path."},
    {"name": "time_horizon_feasibility", "causal_role": "confounder", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Time horizon affects both the mechanisms feasible and the likelihood of achievement; departments choosing longer horizons differ systematically."},
    {"name": "organizational_complexity", "causal_role": "confounder", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Cross-functional/enterprise scope affects both which interventions are used and achievement odds; a genuine common cause surfaced from data."},
    {"name": "metric_type", "causal_role": "confounder", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "The metric used (turnover rate vs sales) influences both the mechanism and the baseline difficulty of achievement."},
    {"name": "resource_constraint_signal", "causal_role": "confounder", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Resource constraints plausibly cause both the intervention chosen and the achievement outcome; a classic common cause."},
    {"name": "change_adoption_mechanism", "causal_role": "mediator", "named_in_query": false, "rationale": "Adoption of change (process/technology/behavioral) sits on the causal path between the intervention mechanism and achievement; adjusting for it would block the effect, so it is a mediator, not a confounder."}
  ],
  "treatment_present": true,
  "treatment_columns": ["intervention_mechanism_type"],
  "confounders": [
    {"name": "goal_scope_domain", "named_in_query": false, "plausibility": 0.6},
    {"name": "goal_quantification_specificity", "named_in_query": false, "plausibility": 0.5},
    {"name": "time_horizon_feasibility", "named_in_query": false, "plausibility": 0.65},
    {"name": "organizational_complexity", "named_in_query": false, "plausibility": 0.7},
    {"name": "metric_type", "named_in_query": false, "plausibility": 0.55},
    {"name": "resource_constraint_signal", "named_in_query": false, "plausibility": 0.7}
  ],
  "confounder_quality": 0.6,
  "rationale": "The added columns do establish a causal estimation setup: intervention_mechanism_type serves as an explicit treatment (candidate cause), and several variables (organizational_complexity, resource_constraint_signal, time_horizon_feasibility, goal_scope_domain, metric_type, goal_quantification_specificity) function as plausible common causes of both the treatment and the outcome. Crucially, none of these confounders were named or implied in the sparse query ('Why do goal achievement rates differ across departments?'), so they demonstrate genuine surfacing from the data/text rather than query-copying — evidence of the capability under test. The main weakness is change_adoption_mechanism, which is a mediator on the intervention→achievement path and would bias the attribution if adjusted for. Overall a solid but imperfect causal-attribution structure, hence a moderate confounder_quality of 0.6."
}
